questions.question: Where was the 30th Senior Women’s National Football Championship – Rajmata Jijabai Trophy final match played?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narainpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The final match of the **30th Senior Women’s National Football Championship**, officially designated as the **Rajmata Jijabai Trophy**, was held in **Narainpur**, **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The championship match took place at the **Ramakrishna Mission Ashrama Ground** on **May 15, 2024**, marking a significant sporting event for the **Bastar division**.
 
• **Manipur** emerged victorious in the final by defeating **Haryana** with a score of **2-0**, showcasing their continued dominance in domestic football.
 
• This win represents the **22nd title** for **Manipur**, making them the most successful state team in the history of the **Senior Women’s National Football Championship**.
 
• The goals for the winning side were netted by **Phanjoubam Nirmala Devi** and **S. Lynda Kom**, ensuring the victory during the ninety-minute regulation time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajmata Jijabai Trophy**:

 
 
• The **All India Football Federation (AIFF)** rebranded the **Senior Women’s National Football Championship** to honor **Rajmata Jijabai**, the mother of the legendary Maratha ruler **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj**.
 
• This rebranding initiative was implemented starting from the **2023-24** season to celebrate women’s leadership and legacy in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Organization**:
 
 
• The **final round** of the competition featured **12 teams** split into two groups, with **Chhattisgarh** serving as the host state for the matches held in **Raipur** and **Narainpur**.
 
• The event is a critical talent identification platform for the **Indian National Women’s Team**, managed by the **AIFF**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• The **Senior Women’s National Football Championship** was inaugurated in **1991** to provide a competitive stage for women athletes across **Indian states** and **Union Territories**.
 
• While **Manipur** leads with 22 titles, other prominent winners in the tournament’s history include **West Bengal** and **Odisha**.

questions.question: Which of the following classical music instruments did Ustad Bismillah Khan mostly popularise?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shehnai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Bismillah Khan** (1916−2006) was a legendary Indian musician who is credited with elevating the **Shehnai** from a traditional folk instrument to the status of a premier **classical music instrument**.
 
• Born in **Dumraon, Bihar**, he belonged to a family of traditional court musicians and received his initial training under his maternal uncle, **Ali Baksh 'Vilayatu'**, the official Shehnai player at the **Kashi Vishwanath Temple** in **Varanasi**.
 
• He gained nationwide recognition after his performance at the **All India Radio** (Lucknow) in **1938**, which proved to be a turning point for both the artist and the instrument.
 
• He famously performed at the **Red Fort** on **15th August 1947**, greeting the newly independent nation with his music after **Jawaharlal Nehru's** 'Tryst with Destiny' speech.
 
• For his unparalleled contribution to Indian music, he was conferred with the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, in **2001**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Veena**

 
 
• An ancient **plucked string instrument** associated with **Goddess Saraswati**; prominent exponents include **S. Balachander** and **Asad Ali Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Sitar**
 
 
• A dominant stringed instrument in **Hindustani classical music**, globally popularized by icons like **Pandit Ravi Shankar** and **Ustad Vilayat Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Tabla**
 
 
• A pair of **percussion twin drums** essential to North Indian music; notable maestros include **Ustad Zakir Hussain**, **Pandit Kishan Maharaj**, and **Ustad Allah Rakha**.

questions.question: Which of the following cities experiences the retreat of Monsoon last?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chennai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **retreat of the monsoon** is a gradual process that begins in the northwestern states of India, such as Rajasthan, around **September 1**. As the **Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)** moves southward, the high-pressure system begins to dominate over the landmass.
 
• By **mid-October**, the **South-West Monsoon** withdraws completely from the northern half of the Indian peninsula. The withdrawal occurs much later in the southern parts because the pressure gradient shifts slowly toward the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• **Chennai**, situated on the **Coromandel Coast**, experiences the withdrawal of the South-West Monsoon last among the given options. While the rest of the country sees a dry spell, the retreating winds pick up moisture from the **Bay of Bengal** and cause significant rainfall in **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The period from **October to December** is characterized by the **North-East Monsoon** in Chennai. This phase is essentially the retreating phase of the South-West Monsoon, making it the city where the monsoon influence lingers the longest before completely withdrawing by **late December**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jaipur**

 
 
• Located in the northwestern state of **Rajasthan**, Jaipur is one of the earliest cities to witness the retreat, usually starting in the **first week of September**.
 
 
 
• **Ahmedabad**
 
 
• Being in **Gujarat**, the monsoon retreat reaches Ahmedabad by the **end of September**, as the winds move away from the western plains toward the central peninsula.
 
 
 
• **Mumbai**
 
 
• The withdrawal of the monsoon from **Maharashtra** and Mumbai generally occurs between **October 5 and October 10**, significantly earlier than the final retreat from the southeastern coast.
 
 
 
• **Retreating Monsoon Characteristics**
 
 
• This season is marked by **clear skies** and a rise in temperature, often referred to as **October Heat**. While the land is still moist, the high temperature and humidity make the weather oppressive.

questions.question: The Ramosi Revolt was led by which tribal leader in 1822 against Britishers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittur Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ramosi Revolt** occurred in **1822** in the **Western Ghats** of **Maharashtra** under the leadership of **Chittur Singh** (also known as **Chittar Singh**).
 
• The **Ramosis** were hill tribes who historically served as the lower-tier police and military guards under the **Maratha Empire**.
 
• The primary cause of the rebellion was the socio-economic distress caused by the **British East India Company** following the final defeat of the **Peshwa** in **1818** and the subsequent annexation of the **Maratha** territories.
 
• High **land revenue assessments** and harsh methods of collection deprived the tribal community of their traditional livelihoods and forest rights.
 
• In **1822**, the **Ramosis** revolted by plundering the region around **Satara** and seizing several local forts to challenge British authority.
 
• The revolt continued intermittently until **1826**, eventually leading the British to adopt a policy of conciliation by granting them **land grants** and recruiting them into the **Hill Police**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Veer Surendra Sai**:

 
 
• He was a significant resistance leader from **Odisha** who fought against the **British** during the **Sambalpur Uprising**.
 
• He spearheaded the struggle from **1827** to **1864**, particularly active during the **Revolt of 1857**, to protect the rights of the native Chauhan dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Bakshi Jagabandhu**:
 
 
• He was the commander of the forces of the Raja of **Khurda** and the leader of the **Paika Rebellion** in **1817**.
 
• The rebellion in **Odisha** was an early armed protest against the **British East India Company's** exploitative land and salt policies.
 
 
 
• **Kittur Chennamma**:
 
 
• She was the **Rani** of **Kittur**, a princely state in present-day **Karnataka**.
 
• She led an armed rebellion against the **British** in **1824** in defiance of the **Doctrine of Lapse** to preserve the independence of her state.

questions.question: On which date was Engineers’ Day observed in India in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 September**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Engineers' Day** is celebrated in **India** annually on **15 September** to commemorate the birth anniversary of **Sir Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya**, one of India's greatest engineers.
 
• The celebration of this day was officially designated by the **Government of India** in **1968** to recognize his monumental contributions to **nation-building** and the field of **civil engineering**.
 
• **Sir M. Visvesvaraya**, often referred to as **Sir M.V.**, was born on **15 September 1860** in **Muddenahalli**, located in the present-day state of **Karnataka**.
 
• The day aims to inspire the **engineering community** across the country and acknowledge their role in **innovation**, **infrastructure development**, and **technological progress**.
 
• In **2025**, the tradition continues to honor his legacy as a visionary **engineer**, **administrator**, and **statesman**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir M. Visvesvaraya's Achievements:**

 
 
• He served as the **19th Diwan of Mysore** from **1912 to 1918** and was the chief engineer responsible for the construction of the **Krishna Raja Sagara Dam**.
 
• He was awarded India's highest civilian honor, the **Bharat Ratna**, in **1955** for his exceptional service to the nation.
 
• He designed and patented a system of **automatic weir water floodgates**, which were first installed at the **Khadakwasla Reservoir** near **Pune** in **1903** to increase the storage level without damaging the dam.
 
• He played a foundational role in establishing the **Government Engineering College** in **Bangalore** in **1917**, which was later renamed the **University Visvesvaraya College of Engineering (UVCE)**.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• While India celebrates on **15 September**, **World Engineering Day for Sustainable Development** is observed globally on **4 March** by **UNESCO**.
 
• Countries like **Sri Lanka** and **Tanzania** also observe **Engineers' Day** on **15 September** in honor of **Sir M. Visvesvaraya**.

questions.question: In which state was the 22ⁿd All India TDS Conference organised to review Income Tax Act amendments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **22nd All India TDS Conference** was successfully organized in **Indore**, located in the state of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The primary agenda of the conference was to conduct a comprehensive review of the recent **Income Tax Act amendments** specifically pertaining to **Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)** and **Tax Collected at Source (TCS)**.
 
• The event served as a critical platform for **Income Tax Officers** and **Commissioners (TDS)** from various regions across India to discuss administrative strategies and enhance tax compliance.
 
• Significant focus was placed on the **digital transformation** of tax processes, including the use of **Data Analytics** to identify non-compliance and streamline the **rectification process** for deductors.
 
• The conference emphasized the role of **TDS** as a major contributor to the **Direct Tax** collection, often accounting for nearly **40% to 50%** of the total direct tax revenue in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income Tax Act, 1961**:

 
 
• This is the **statutory framework** that governs the administration, collection, and recovery of **Direct Taxes** in India.
 
• **TDS mechanism**: It was introduced to collect taxes at the very source of income generation, ensuring a **regular cash flow** to the **Government of India**.
 
 
 
• **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)**:
 
 
• The **CBDT** is a statutory authority functioning under the **Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963**.
 
• It provides essential inputs for **policy making** and planning of direct taxes and is responsible for the administration of direct tax laws through the **Income Tax Department**.
 
 
 
• **TDS Provisions**:
 
 
• Specific sections like **Section 192** (Salary), **Section 194J** (Professional Fees), and **Section 194C** (Contracts) are frequently amended in the **Union Budget** to widen the tax base.

questions.question: The inaugural railway line in the Indian subcontinent was opened in 1853 between between which two locations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay and Thane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first passenger train in the **Indian subcontinent** was officially flagged off on **April 16, 1853**, marking the beginning of the railway era in **British India**.
 
• The train journey commenced from **Bori Bunder** (now known as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus) and concluded at **Thane**, covering a distance of approximately **34 kilometers**.
 
• This inaugural run was powered by three steam locomotives named **Sahib**, **Sindh**, and **Sultan**, which were manufactured in **England**.
 
• The train consisted of **14 carriages** and carried about **400 passengers**, departing at **3:35 PM** to a **21-gun salute**.
 
• The operation was managed by the **Great Indian Peninsula Railway (GIPR)**, a company incorporated by an **Act of the British Parliament** in **1849**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Dalhousie**: Served as the **Governor-General of India** from **1848 to 1856** and is celebrated as the **Father of Indian Railways** for his vision in connecting the country through rail.
 
• **Growth of the Network**:
 
 
• In **Eastern India**, the first train ran from **Howrah to Hooghly** on **August 15, 1854**, covering **24 miles**.
 
• In **Southern India**, the first line was opened by the **Madras Railway Company** on **July 1, 1856**, between **Veyasarpadi and Walajah Road**.
 
 
 
• **Structural Significance**: **Bori Bunder** was later reconstructed into the **Victoria Terminus** in **1888** to commemorate **Queen Victoria’s Golden Jubilee** and is today a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• **First Railway Proposals**: While the first train ran in **1853**, the earliest proposals for a railway in **India** were made in **Madras** in **1832**, primarily for industrial transport.
